Key Finding: Customer segments differ in ordering behavior, spending, and engagement.
Business Implication: Customer strategies can be tailored according to segment value and behavior.

Key Finding: Restaurant clusters differ in revenue, order volume, ratings, and operational performance.
Business Implication: Operational attention can be prioritized toward underperforming restaurant groups.

Key Finding: VADER achieved stronger sentiment classification performance than the TF-IDF + Naive Bayes approach.
Business Implication: Automated sentiment monitoring can help identify customer experience issues.

Key Finding: Delivery delays and food quality/freshness are the two largest complaint themes.
Business Implication: Reducing delivery delays and improving food freshness should be priority areas.

Key Finding: Delivery distance and preparation time are the strongest predictors of delivery time.
Business Implication: Improving preparation efficiency and managing long-distance deliveries can reduce delivery times.

Key Finding: Demand is relatively similar between weekdays and weekends, but varies by specific days and hours.
Business Implication: Capacity planning should focus on specific high-demand days and hours rather than weekends alone.
